results.question: Does the Claude platform train on my data?
results.answer:
**No — by default, the Claude platform does not train on your data.**

Here is the specific policy for Syracuse University users:

> *"By default, the data that Syracuse University users upload and the chat sessions they create are not used to train any of the Claude platform AI models."*

There is one exception: **if you explicitly report feedback or bugs to Claude**, then Claude may use your submission to train AI models [[488210484]].

### Personalization Features (separate from training)
Claude does have **personalization features** that are distinct from model training. These allow the platform to remember you and reference prior chat sessions/projects when generating new outputs. You can configure or disable these settings at the [Claude Settings page](https://claude.ai/settings/features). More details are available at [Anthropic's Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features) [[488210484]].

---

**Sources:**
- [Claude - Frequently Asked Questions](https://answers.atlassian.syr.edu/wiki/spaces/ITSAI/pages/488210484/Claude+-+Frequently+Asked+Questions) [[488210484]]

results.question: Can I use Claude while traveling outside the US?
results.answer:
Great question! Here's what you need to know about using Claude while traveling internationally:

## Traveling Abroad with Claude

**Yes, you may be able to use Claude abroad — but it depends on the country.** Anthropic restricts access from certain countries, and this is an important consideration [[488210484]]:

- ⚠️ **Attempting to access Claude from a prohibited country may result in your Syracuse University Claude account being banned by Anthropic.** This is a significant risk, as SU cannot intervene in Anthropic's ban decisions [[488210484]].
- ✅ **Check the country list before you travel:** Anthropic maintains a full list of supported countries here: [Anthropic | Supported Countries](https://www.anthropic.com/supported-countries)

## If Your Account Gets Banned

If your SU Claude account is banned due to access from a restricted country, you'll need to **appeal directly to Anthropic** through their support system [[488210484]]:
- **Appeal link:** https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241253-safeguards-warnings-and-appeals
- Be honest about what happened and explain your intended use case.
- Note that appeals are reviewed by Anthropic's Trust & Safety team, and **approval is not guaranteed**. SU's Enterprise agreement does not give the university any influence over ban decisions.

**Bottom line:** Always check [Anthropic's supported countries list](https://www.anthropic.com/supported-countries) before traveling to ensure your destination is permitted. Accessing Claude from a restricted country risks a permanent account ban.

---

**Sources:**
- [Claude - Frequently Asked Questions](https://answers.atlassian.syr.edu/wiki/spaces/ITSAI/pages/488210484/Claude+-+Frequently+Asked+Questions) [[488210484]]

results.question: What is mentorAI and how is it different from regular Claude?
results.answer:
Here's a comprehensive breakdown of **mentorAI** and how it differs from **regular Claude** at Syracuse University:

---

## 🤖 What is mentorAI?

**mentorAI** (sometimes called "Clementine") is a **Syracuse University-run AI platform** — separate from Claude.ai — that enables AI-powered, personalized assistants (called "mentors") for students, faculty, and staff. You can access it at [mentor.ai.syr.edu](https://mentor.ai.syr.edu/) [[544505857]].

It is purpose-built for **academic use cases**, with two main audiences:

### 🎓 For Students:
- **Create custom study mentors** tailored to your courses and textbooks
- **Adaptive learning paths** that adjust to your pace and understanding
- **Verified, cited answers** grounded in your own course materials [[544505857]]

### 👩‍🏫 For Faculty:
- Build **course-specific AI teaching assistants** to handle repetitive questions and FAQs
- Get **AI-assisted assignment review and feedback**
- Generate **lesson plans, quizzes, and materials** quickly
- All mentors use only **faculty-approved content**, ensuring accuracy and academic integrity [[544505857]]

---

## ⚖️ How is mentorAI Different from Regular Claude?

| Feature | Regular Claude (claude.ai) | mentorAI (mentor.ai.syr.edu) |
|---|---|---|
| **Platform owner** | Anthropic (licensed by SU) | Syracuse University-run |
| **Primary purpose** | General-purpose AI assistant | Personalized academic mentors grounded in course materials |
| **Usage limits** | Subject to monthly caps; Opus/Sonnet use more allocation | **Higher usage limits** than Claude [[488210484]] |
| **Extra capabilities** | Web search, M365 connectors, code execution | Additional tools like **screen sharing** [[488210484]] |
| **Content grounding** | Trained on broad internet knowledge | Answers grounded in **your specific uploaded course materials**, with citations [[544505857]] |
| **Premium seat needed?** | A premium seat ($2,400/yr) is required for higher limits & Claude Code | No separate premium seat requirement mentioned |
| **Best for** | Research, writing, coding, analysis, broad tasks | Course-specific tutoring, teaching assistance, academic mentoring |

---

## 💡 When Should You Use mentorAI vs. Claude?

The Claude FAQ explicitly recommends mentorAI as an alternative if you **anticipate needing higher usage limits and don't want to pay for a Claude premium seat**. mentorAI includes Anthropic/Claude models under the hood but offers higher limits and additional tools like screen sharing that Claude.ai doesn't provide [[488210484]].

---

results.question: How do I create a new mentor on the Clementine platform?
results.answer:
Here's a step-by-step guide on how to create a new mentor on the Clementine (mentorAI) platform [[535068673]]:

---

## 🧑‍🏫 Creating a New Mentor on mentorAI

### Step 1: Start a New Mentor
- From your **dashboard**, click the **"New Mentor"** button.

---

### Step 2: Input Mentor Information
Fill in the following fields:

1. **Name** — Enter the mentor's name. This is the primary identifier mentees will see when searching.
2. **Description** — Write a brief bio covering the mentor's background, skills, and what type of mentorship they offer (e.g., career advice, skill development).
3. **Category** — Select the appropriate category based on the mentor's expertise (e.g., Astronomy, Art, Anthropology). This helps mentees find relevant mentors.
4. **Mentor Visibility** — Choose who can see the mentor: all students, select groups, or keep it private.
5. **Image** *(optional)* — Upload a professional profile picture to make the profile more engaging and relatable.

---

### Step 3: Configure Prompts
Set up how the mentor will interact with mentees:

1. **System Prompts** — Review and edit the pre-populated prompts that govern how the mentor interacts. Customize them to fit the mentor's style or focus areas.
2. **Proactive Prompts** — Add prompts designed to initiate discussions with mentees. Tailor these to encourage specific types of interactions.
3. **Guided Prompts** — Set structured guidance for conversations. Make them relevant to the mentor's expertise and the mentee's needs.

> 💡 **Tip:** Add your custom-configured prompts at the **bottom of the defaults** for more effective mentoring.

---

### Step 4: Save
- Click the **"Save"** button to submit and publish the new mentor profile.

---

For more detailed configuration options (e.g., advanced settings, web crawlers), check out the **mentorAI Settings & Options** page.

---

**Sources:**
- [mentorAI Creating A Mentor](https://answers.atlassian.syr.edu/wiki/spaces/ITSAI/pages/535068673/mentorAI+Creating+A+Mentor) [[535068673]]

results.question: What's MCP at Syracuse and how do I use it?
results.answer:
Here's a comprehensive guide to MCP at Syracuse University:

---

## 🔌 What Is MCP?

**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open-source standard developed by Anthropic that allows Claude to securely connect to and interact with external data sources, tools, and services [[841875458]]. Think of it as the "plugin system" for Claude — it lets Claude read your SharePoint files, query databases, or interact with software like Power BI, all from within the Claude interface [[837517313]].

At SU, MCP powers two distinct types of integrations: **Enterprise Connectors** (managed by ITS) and **Local MCP** (configured by you on your own machine).

---

## 🏢 Enterprise Connectors (ITS-Managed)

These are enabled at the organization level by ITS and appear in your Claude settings once activated.

### ✅ Already Enabled for All SU Users

| Connector | What It Does |
|---|---|
| **Microsoft 365** | Lets Claude search your SharePoint files, OneDrive docs, Teams messages, and Outlook emails [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]] |
| **Atlassian** | Lets Claude read Jira tickets and Confluence pages [[841875458]] |

To activate the M365 connector, go to **Claude Settings → Connectors → Microsoft 365 → Connect**, and sign in with your `netid@syr.edu` account [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

### 📋 Requesting a New Enterprise Connector

If a tool you use has a Claude connector and you want ITS to enable it campus-wide, email **aihelp@syr.edu** with [[841875458]]:

1. The connector name and link to its documentation
2. Your business use case
3. Confirmation of an existing SU vendor contract (if applicable)
4. A **SOC 2 Type II report** from the vendor *(the single most important requirement)*

ITS evaluates requests on: security compliance (SOC 2), existing SU contracts, data classification risk, breadth of campus benefit, and vendor maturity. Requests **will not be approved** without a SOC 2 report or if the connector would expose restricted data (FERPA, HIPAA, PII, etc.) without adequate controls [[841875458]].

---

## 💻 Local MCP (Claude Desktop — User-Configured)

Local MCP lets you connect the **Claude Desktop app** to tools and data running *entirely on your own machine* — no enterprise admin approval required [[837517313]]. This is great for connecting Claude to local apps like Power BI.

### Step-by-Step: Connect Claude Desktop to Power BI

Here's the documented example [[837517313]]:

1. **Install the VS Code Extension** — Search for "Power BI Modeling MCP" in VS Code and install the one published by Microsoft.
2. **Find the `.exe` file** — Navigate to a path like:
   ```
   C:\Users\<YourUsername>\.vscode\extensions\analysis-services.powerbi-modeling-mcp-0.1.9-win32-x64\server
   ```
3. **Copy the path** — Hold Shift, right-click the `.exe`, and select "Copy as path."
4. **Edit Claude Desktop's config** — Open the Claude Desktop app, click the **Edit Config** button, then add:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "powerbi-modeling-mcp": {
         "command": "paste your path here",
         "args": ["--start"],
         "env": {}
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   > ⚠️ Use **double backslashes** (`\\`) instead of single ones (`\`) in the path.
5. **Reboot** — Restart your computer and reopen Claude Desktop. The MCP will appear in the interface.
6. **Use it** — Open your Power BI report, then in Claude Desktop type: *"Connect to the open Power BI desktop file"* and Claude will assist with modeling tasks.

You can add multiple local MCPs by separating them with commas in the `mcpServers` block [[837517313]].

---

## 📁 Filesystem Connector (Bonus: Local File Access)

Claude Desktop also supports a **Filesystem connector** that lets Claude read, edit, and create files in folders you explicitly grant access to [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. A popular pattern is to use it with SharePoint by adding a SharePoint folder shortcut to your OneDrive ("Add shortcut to My files"), then pointing the connector at your `OneDrive - Syracuse University` path — giving Claude effective access to SharePoint files [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

---

## 🔐 A Note on Data Policy

Even with Local MCP, anything you expose to Claude is still seen by the model. Always follow SU's data-handling guidelines and don't route restricted or confidential university data through unapproved integrations [[841875458]].

---

## Quick Decision Guide

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| Connect Claude to my SharePoint/Teams/Outlook | Enable the **M365 connector** in Claude Settings |
| Connect Claude to Jira or Confluence | Enable the **Atlassian connector** in Claude Settings |
| Connect Claude to another SaaS tool | Email **aihelp@syr.edu** with a connector request |
| Connect Claude Desktop to a local app (e.g., Power BI) | Configure a **local MCP server** in Claude Desktop's config file |
| Have Claude work with local or SharePoint files | Install Claude Desktop and enable the **Filesystem connector** |

---

## Sources

## Connecting Claude to Microsoft 365

The Claude M365 connector lets Claude access your **Microsoft Teams messages, Outlook emails, SharePoint and OneDrive documents**, and more — giving Claude context from your existing M365 resources [[544210961]].

### Step-by-Step Instructions

1. **Log into Claude** using your Syracuse University account (`netid@syr.edu`) [[544210961]].

results.question: Can I use Google NotebookLM at Syracuse, and what can it do?
results.answer:
Yes! Google NotebookLM is available at Syracuse University, and it's a powerful research and study tool. Here's a full rundown:

---

## ✅ Is NotebookLM Approved at SU?

Yes. NotebookLM is part of Syracuse University's Google Workspace for Education suite, covered by the Google Workspace for Education Terms of Service with enterprise-grade security and privacy controls [[530546723]]. It is accessible through your SU Google account (`NetID@g.syr.edu`).

---

## 📋 What Can NotebookLM Do?

NotebookLM is a **source-grounded AI tool** — it only works from documents *you* upload, not from the general web (unless you use Discover Sources). Here's what it offers:

### Core Features
- **Summarize Readings** — Generate short study notes or overviews from articles, PDFs, and case studies [[530546723]]
- **Ask Targeted Questions** — Chat with your uploaded materials (e.g., "Compare the main arguments from each source") [[530546723]]
- **Discover Sources** — Find trusted web content related to a topic, or use "I'm feeling curious" to auto-build a notebook [[530546723]]
- **Configure Chat Style** — Choose *Guided Learning*, *Default*, or *Custom* modes, and adjust response length [[530546723]]
- **Save Notes** — Save responses or write your own notes, and even convert them into new AI-queryable sources [[530546723]]

### Studio Features (Advanced Tools)
| Feature | What It Does |
|---|---|
| 🎧 **Audio Overview** | Generates an AI podcast (Deep Dive, Brief, or Debate format) from your sources |
| 🎥 **Video Overview** | Creates a short video summarizing key ideas |
| 🧠 **Mind Map** | Visualizes connections between concepts and themes |
| 📊 **Reports** | Compiles sources into a structured written briefing |
| 🗂️ **Flashcards** | Auto-generates flashcards from your notes |
| ❓ **Quiz** | Tests your comprehension with custom questions |

[[530546723]]

---

## 📁 What Can You Upload?

- **Google Workspace files:** Google Docs, Google Slides
- **Documents:** PDFs, text files, Markdown files
- **Web content:** URLs (visible text only; no paywalled pages), copy-pasted text
- **Multimedia:** Audio files (MP3, WAV), YouTube URLs (public videos with captions only)

**Limits:** Up to **50 sources per notebook**, each up to **500,000 words** or **200MB** [[530546723]]

---

## 🔒 Privacy & Data Handling

- Your uploaded files, chats, and outputs **will NOT be reviewed by human reviewers** [[530546723]]
- They **will NOT be used to train Google's AI models** [[530546723]]
- The service supports compliance with **FERPA and COPPA** [[530546723]]

---

## 🤝 Collaboration & Sharing

- Notebooks can be **shared within the Syracuse University domain only** [[530546723]]
- Collaborators with editor permissions can work in **real time** [[530546723]]
- Study aids like flashcards and quizzes can be **shared via a simple link** [[530546723]]

---

## 🆘 Need Help?

Contact the **ITS Help Desk**: 315-443-2677 | help@syr.edu [[530546723]]

---

results.question: Who has access to my AI usage data at Syracuse?
results.answer:
Great question — and the answer depends on which AI tool you're using. Here's what the official Syracuse University documentation says about who can access your AI usage data:

---

## 👤 Authorized SU IT Staff

Across **Claude Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot, and Google Gemini**, the policy is consistent: your data is **"inherently accessible to authorized IT staff"** for support, security, and maintenance purposes. This access is governed by SU's **IT Resources Acceptable Use policy** and the **Information Security Framework** [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

---

## 🔍 Per-Tool Breakdown

### 🟣 Claude Enterprise
- SU IT staff can access your data for support/security/maintenance.
- **Anthropic does not use your chats to train models** by default. The only exception is if you explicitly submit feedback or a bug report.
- All chats are **retained for 2 years** — even deleted items remain on the platform during that window [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

### 🔵 Microsoft Copilot
- SU IT staff can access data within the M365 environment.
- Conversations are stored in a **hidden folder in your M365 mailbox**, and are **recoverable/searchable by admins for up to 30 days** after you delete them (or longer, depending on your mailbox's retention policies).
- **Microsoft does not use your SU account interactions to train AI models** [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

### 🟡 Google Gemini
- SU IT staff access is governed by the same Acceptable Use and Information Security Framework policies.
- Notably, **Google personnel do not human-review or access your chats** to improve AI models.
- Gemini only accesses Google Drive files you **explicitly open, reference, or share** in a session — not your entire Drive [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

### 🟠 mentorAI (Clementine Platform)
- The SU corpus does not currently publish a detailed data-retention, training, or access FAQ for mentorAI comparable to the other tools [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

---

## ✅ Key Takeaways

| Who | Can They See Your AI Data? |
|---|---|
| Authorized SU IT Staff | ✅ Yes — for support, security, maintenance |
| AI Vendor (Anthropic, Microsoft, Google) | ❌ Not for model training (opt-out by default) |
| Google Human Reviewers | ❌ Not for Gemini at SU |
| Other SU users | ❌ Not unless you explicitly share |

> ⚠️ **Be cautious** about sharing Claude Projects or Artifacts with others — shared items may expose data to those you share with [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

---

results.question: Where can I find example uses of Claude for academic work?
results.answer:
Syracuse University has a dedicated **"Example Uses"** section within the Claude knowledge base. Here's a summary of all five example use pages available for academic and professional work:

---

## 📚 Example Uses of Claude at SU

### 1. 🎓 Study Project
Create a Study Project in Claude to master your coursework. Upload lecture slides, PDFs, or notes and ask Claude to:
- Summarize chapters into flashcards
- Explain key concepts from slides
- Generate quizzes on uploaded material

**How to start:** Click "Learn" or "Study project" from the Claude home screen and upload your class materials [[511279124]].

---

### 2. 🔬 AI Research Assistant
Use Claude as a personal research assistant for academic papers and literature reviews. Key features include:
- Upload up to **5 documents per conversation** (PDFs, Word docs, research articles)
- Use **Projects** to organize readings by course — Claude remembers them across conversations
- **Multi-document analysis** for comparing sources or building literature reviews
- Generate editable **Artifacts** for outlines, summaries, and annotated bibliographies
- **Extended Thinking** mode for deeper analysis of complex research questions

Example prompts include summarizing articles, comparing two sources side-by-side, creating a literature review outline, and extracting key quotes [[572194844]].

---

### 3. 💼 Career Project
Prepare for internships and job applications by uploading your resume and a job description. Claude can:
- Tailor your resume for a specific role
- Draft personalized cover letters
- Help you practice behavioral interview questions and research companies [[511246346]].

---

### 4. 📝 Drafting Emails
Write clear, professional emails fast. Claude can draft:
- Thank-you emails to professors or recruiters
- Emails to professors about extensions or clarifications
- Group project coordination messages
- Internship follow-up emails

**Pro tip:** Ask Claude to "put it in an artifact" so the draft appears in a separate, easily editable panel [[516325410]].

---

### 5. 📋 Meeting Summaries
Turn Zoom (.txt) or Teams (.docx) transcripts into actionable summaries. Claude can produce:
- Formal meeting minutes
- Topic-based summaries
- Action items and task lists
- Quick 5-minute takeaways

SU even provides a pre-configured **[Meeting Transcripts Project](https://claude.ai/project/0199e821-95e3-74d4-b2ec-826cf3711895)** with prompts already set up [[500236296]].

---

> ⚠️ **Reminder:** Always review Claude's output for accuracy, never include FERPA-protected or sensitive data, and cite original sources in your academic work.

---
